home.body: Four armies move around one crossboard. Earn points, watch every approach, and decide when to take the lead.
home.rulesTitle: A familiar game, from four sides

tutorial.title: Read the crossboard
tutorial.subtitle: A short, interactive table lesson
tutorial.wrong: Not quite. Try another square or answer.

steps.welcome: Four players share one board. Each player moves a full chess army from one side of the cross.
steps.shape: The board is a 14 by 14 grid with each 3 by 3 corner removed. The open center joins all four wings.
steps.turns: Red starts. Play then moves clockwise: Red, Blue, Yellow, Green. Who moves after Red?
steps.pieces: Rooks, Knights, Bishops, Queens and Kings use their familiar chess moves, clipped to the crossboard. Move the Red Knight from e1 to d3.
steps.red-pawn: Red Pawns move north toward the center. Move the Pawn from d2 to d4.
steps.directions: Each Pawn moves toward the center from its own side. Which way does Green move?
steps.score: Captures earn points: Pawn 1, Knight 3, Bishop 5, Rook 5, Queen 9. Capture the Blue Queen with the Red Rook.
steps.promotion: A Pawn reaching its own eighth rank becomes a Queen automatically. Move d7 to d8.
steps.special: Castling moves the King two spaces toward its home Rook when the path is clear and safe. En passant is available only to the very next seat after a two-space Pawn move. Kings are never captured.
steps.elimination: Checkmate and stalemate are resolved when that seat’s turn begins. Eliminated pieces stay as inert blockers and give no capture points.
steps.finish: The game ends when three seats are eliminated. Repetition, bare Kings, and fifty quiet rounds award points to the active seats.
